hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Trump says US may strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain very soon
brief.h: Speaking at the White House on Friday, Trump repeated a threat he first made in mid-July against the deeply buried tunnel complex about 1.5km south of Natanz - hours after telling reporters the six-month campaign is 'small potatoes for us' and endorsing Vance's refusal to call it a war, in a conflict the administration's own figures put at more than $37.5bn and 18 American service members dead.
brief.t: Two statements pointing in opposite directions on the same afternoon is not incoherence, it is division of labour: the Pickaxe threat is aimed at Tehran and the 'not a war' line is aimed at Congress. The adjective is doing legal work. 'Military conflict' is the vocabulary an executive reaches for when it does not want a War Powers clock restarted, a fresh authorisation vote scheduled six weeks before a midterm, or a casualty count sitting in the same headline as the word war. Notice also what the threat is NOT: Pickaxe Mountain has been threatened publicly since July and not hit, which is the behaviour of a target being used as leverage rather than a target being serviced.
brief.context: The rail is the 1973 War Powers Resolution and fifty years of executives calling things hostilities, operations and conflicts to avoid triggering its clocks - the naming fight is older than this war and the government almost always wins it, because the courts treat it as a political question. The deciding desk is not the podium: it is the targeting shop at CENTCOM and, behind it, the munitions inventory - which is precisely the subject of the leak hunt in the card below. Base rate on publicly threatened, deeply buried, never-inspected sites is that they are struck late or not at all, because a hardened target under a hundred metres of rock is the one thing a bombing campaign cannot promise to finish, and an unfulfilled threat keeps its coercive value. What changes the read: a strike executed, or an IAEA access agreement covering the site.

angles.effect: Gains the whole benefit of the word - a 'military conflict' does not restart a War Powers clock, does not force an authorisation vote before November, and does not read as a war next to a casualty figure
Pays: every month the naming holds is a month the vote it wants is never scheduled, and the framing is the reason it is not

angles.party: US service members and the 18 dead
angles.effect: Pay the literal cost the adjective is shrinking - and the $37.5bn and the death toll are the administration's own numbers, not an opponent's
Gains a free line - a superpower that calls six months small has not ended it - while paying the risk that a war officially downgraded is politically cheaper to widen

dec.kill: A War Powers or Article II notification to Congress that uses the word war, a scheduled AUMF vote, or an actual strike on the Pickaxe complex. Any one of the three ends the framing.

consp.claim: That the Pickaxe threat is deliberately never executed because the site is already empty and the repetition exists to keep an escalation premium alive, and - in the louder version running in the happening threads - that Iran has raised the black flag of vengeance over Hormuz and a general war is days away.
consp.spread: A dedicated /pol/ happening thread claiming Iran has raised the black flag, alongside /pig/ Persia Israel General now at its 2037th edition, whose own header mocks the timeline with 'Day 187 of the 4-Day Special Military Operation to Regime Change Iran'.
consp.read: Two frames stacked. The first is the standing 'the threat is the product' reading, which has a checkable kernel: the site has been openly threatened since mid-July and remains unstruck, and specialist imagery analysts have assessed it as not yet operational. The second is ordinary happening-thread escalation, and the board's own sarcastic day-count is evidence its regulars have learned to discount it.

brief.head: Pentagon polygraphs about 50 Joint Staff members in leak hunt
brief.h: The New York Times reports that investigators put roughly fifty military officers and civilian employees of the Joint Staff through polygraph examinations during August, asking whether they had given classified information to reporters and specifically whether they had disclosed the state of diminished US munitions stocks - with spokesman Sean Parnell saying only that the department does not comment on internal investigations but takes leaks extremely seriously.
brief.t: Read this against the card above, because they are the same story from two ends. The administration's public line is that the Iran campaign is small and US forces remain in strong shape; the disclosures it is hunting are about interceptor and precision-munition inventories. A leak hunt is a revealed preference - you strap fifty people to a machine over the fact that hurts, not the fact that embarrasses. And the fact that hurts here is arithmetic: after six months of a shooting campaign, the binding constraint on American options is not resolve, it is magazine depth, and magazine depth is a number that either exists in the logistics directorate's spreadsheets or does not.
brief.context: The rail is that federal national-security work is carved out of the Employee Polygraph Protection Act, so this is lawful - but polygraph results are inadmissible in court and are not accepted as reliable evidence of deception in the scientific literature, which means the instrument's real output is not identification, it is chill. The base rate on leak-hunt polygraphs producing a prosecutable name is very close to zero; the base rate on them producing silence is high, and silence is the deliverable. The deciding desk is the Secretary's office, not the services. What would change the read is a munitions supplemental actually sent to Congress, because the moment you ask for the money you have conceded the shortage.

angles.effect: Gains deterrence without conceding anything - fifty examinations buy months of quiet on the inventory question at no policy cost
Pay career and clearance risk to an instrument that is not evidence, over disclosures that in most cases concern readiness rather than sources or methods
Pay: the number they would need to size an interceptor supplemental is exactly the number being suppressed, so the oversight body is funding a war on stale inventory data
Gain eventually - a shortage that stays hidden until it breaks tends to break as an emergency multiyear procurement at emergency prices

dec.kill: A munitions supplemental with a named interceptor line item, or an indictment naming a leaker. The first concedes the shortage; the second means the polygraphs actually worked.

consp.claim: That the polygraphs are the confirmation that America has physically run out of interceptors, and that the Selective Service System quietly wargaming a draft is the next step in the same sequence.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread built on a Military Times report that Selective Service wants to build a computer model of a draft because it fears its new pool plans will not work, now being read together with the leak-hunt reporting.
consp.read: The 'they are preparing for something they will not announce' frame, applied to two genuine documents. The checkable kernel is real - Selective Service modernisation and the munitions-stock leaks are both independently reported - but the join between them is inference, and draft-machinery updates are routine bureaucratic maintenance that has preceded no draft in fifty years.

brief.head: US takes Venezuela oil stake as penny warrants shielded from dilution
brief.h: A US official told Reuters on Thursday that Washington's 35 per cent position in North American Blue Energy Partners is held as penny warrants with anti-dilution protection - letting the government collect dividends before it ever exercises - in the same week CNN reported that federal prosecutors in Miami closed their money-laundering investigation into NABEP's controller, Alejandro Betancourt, on instructions from the deputy attorney general's office.
brief.t: The structure is the story, so name it. A penny warrant is the right to buy equity for essentially nothing, and anti-dilution means that right survives every capital raise the venture makes - and a 100-year concession over seventeen fields with 65 billion barrels of claimed reserves will need billions in raises. So Washington has arranged to put in no capital, carry no development risk, keep the upside, and take dividends in the meantime. That is not an oil deal; it is a sovereign wealth position, and it is being run out of a Pentagon financing office rather than Treasury. Then follow the payment for the intermediary: not cash, but a closed criminal file.
brief.context: The rail is the Office of Strategic Capital, a Defense Department credit and equity vehicle built for critical-minerals supply chains and now retrofitted as an equity desk for foreign hydrocarbons - the retrofit is the tell, because it means no new statute was needed and no appropriation vote was taken. Follow the physical board underneath: US Gulf refiners are configured for heavy sour crude, Venezuelan barrels are the historic feed, and Canadian heavy is the substitute whose discount widens if the Venezuelan stream ever returns. But note the clock the announcement does not mention - extra-heavy, infrastructure-starved barrels need diluent, upgraders, power and dredged ports, and take three to seven years to reach meaningful volume. The base rate on 100-year concessions signed under sanctions and military pressure is that successor governments campaign on tearing them up.

angles.effect: Gains a costless call option - penny warrants need almost no capital, anti-dilution preserves the 35 per cent through every raise, and dividends flow before exercise
Gains the largest concession of his career and, per CNN, the closure of a federal money-laundering investigation - the broker was paid in legal jeopardy removed
Pay: they fund the development capex while a non-diluting 35 per cent holder sits above them in the stack and takes dividends
Pays the sovereignty price - a century of rights over seventeen fields conceded under sanctions and military pressure is precisely the contract the next government runs against
Pay on a delay - a restored Venezuelan heavy stream at the Gulf Coast is the direct substitute for Alberta's discounted barrel

dec.kill: A funded capex commitment with a named operator and a first-oil date turns this into industry; the warrants quietly lapsing unexercised means it was an announcement with a legal favour attached.

consp.claim: That the whole Venezuela operation - the boat strikes, the pressure campaign, the deal - was an oil seizure from the start, and that the quietly closed Betancourt investigation is the receipt proving the intermediary was bought rather than recruited.
consp.spread: Running hard in the long-running /pol/ Trump-corruption catalogue thread and picked up on X off the CNN and Semafor reporting.
consp.read: The 'the real reason is the oil' frame, which is the oldest read in the file and is right often enough to deserve checking rather than dismissal. The kernel here is not fringe: CNN reports the probe was closed on orders from the deputy attorney general's office while officials worked to enlist Betancourt, and Semafor reports scrutiny of the Pentagon office that booked the stake. What the frame adds is intent and sequencing, which the reporting does not yet establish.

brief.head: Panama Canal cuts daily slots again as El Nino drains Gatun Lake
brief.h: The canal authority reduced Neopanamax slots to nine and Panamax slots to twenty-five from 3 September and will cut Panamax again to twenty-three on 15 September, down from a normal thirty-six transits a day, after cumulative rainfall across the watershed ran roughly 34 per cent below the historical average from May through August and inflows roughly 44 per cent below.
brief.t: This is the second chokepoint on our board this week and the only one where nobody is shooting - which makes it the cleanest illustration of what a chokepoint actually is. Bab al-Mandab is being repriced by underwriters because of a war; Panama is being repriced by rainfall; a freight desk cannot tell the difference, because both arrive as the same thing - fewer slots and a higher price for one. Name the mechanism: the canal is not a waterway, it is a staircase made of fresh water, and every transit spends tens of millions of gallons of Gatun Lake to the sea. The binding constraint is a reservoir, not a hull, and the auction slot is where the scarcity gets a number.
brief.context: The rail is 2023-24, when drought took transits down to about 22 a day and pushed Asia to US East Coast box traffic onto Suez and onto US West Coast ports with a landbridge. That escape route is materially worse now, because Suez sits behind Bab al-Mandab and a war-risk premium, so the two chokepoints are no longer independent - a fact worth holding, because the standard model of global shipping assumes you can always substitute one for the other. The deciding desk is the ACP board, and the number that matters is Gatun's level against its rule curve, not the transit count, which is only the output. Base rate: ACP restrictions of this type have run one to two quarters and reversed with the rains rather than escalating.

angles.effect: Gains on price as it loses on volume - fewer slots put through an auction system means each remaining slot clears higher, which has historically cushioned drought revenue
Pay in freight and in days, and pay it into the pre-Christmas restock window when the schedule has least slack
Pay more than in 2023 - the Suez alternative now carries a war-risk premium, so the usual substitution is not free
Pay in the tail and with no seat - the drinking supply draws on the same watershed, and every gallon locked through is a gallon not stored

dec.kill: Gatun recovering to its rule curve on the November rains with slots restored toward 36 confirms this is El Nino. Restrictions persisting through a normal-rainfall year, or a third consecutive dry season, means the driver is watershed structure and not weather - a different and much worse story.

brief.head: Xi plans to bring a CEO delegation to the Washington summit
brief.h: Reuters reports Xi is assembling an unusually large business delegation for the 24 September summit in Washington - a break from his practice since the 2020 crackdowns on Chinese tech, education and property - while a separate Reuters exclusive says Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will lead the first dedicated US-China AI dialogue of this term in mid-September, an account a White House official disputed by saying no such meeting is currently planned.
brief.t: The revealing fact is not that AI talks may happen, it is whose desk they sit on. Bessent - not State, not Commerce, not a White House AI office - means Washington is treating frontier AI as a financial-statecraft file, filed next to export controls, investment screening and tariff truces, rather than as an arms-control one. That choice predicts the deal shape: access traded for restraint, not verification traded for limits. Xi arriving with CEOs is the mirror image of the same logic - Beijing is offering deal announcements as the summit deliverable because deal announcements are the currency this White House scores in, and because putting private founders back on a state plane is a message to Chinese capital as much as to American.
brief.context: The rail is 2015, when Xi's state visit opened with a Seattle CEO roundtable and closed with a cyber-espionage understanding - the template is old, the deliverable then was also a norms document plus commercial goodwill, and the understanding decayed within three years. The deciding desk on the Chinese side is unresolved and worth watching: Reuters names Vice Premier He Lifeng but flags Ding Xuexiang as an alternative, and which of them appears tells you whether Beijing has filed AI under economics or under ideology. Base rate on this administration's bilateral technology dialogues is tariff truces and communiques rather than binding instruments. The floated American proposal - that US and Chinese labs police themselves and share information on AI-directed cyberattacks - is an ask with no statute behind it on either side.

angles.effect: Gains the optics it wants twice over - CEOs in the room signal to foreign investors that China is open and to Chinese founders that the crackdown era is being wound down
Gains announceable investment numbers before November while keeping deniability, which is exactly what the flat official denial of the AI meeting purchases
Pay: a Treasury-led AI channel puts the file with the department most willing to trade controls for market access
Would carry the actual obligation under a self-policing arrangement - asked to share attack information with no law compelling either of them, and no mechanism if one stops

dec.kill: A named Chinese principal confirmed for the AI session, or a published information-sharing mechanism, turns a floated channel into an instrument. Continued White House denial straight through the 24 September summit means there was never a channel to begin with.

consp.claim: That US-China AI safety cooperation is a cartel with a safety label - two governments agreeing on who is permitted to build frontier models - and that the datacentre build-out underwriting it is being quietly loaded onto household electricity bills.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread arguing datacentres raise consumer power prices, running alongside a well-trafficked thread from a poster blaming an energy-driven rent increase, and echoed on /biz/ around a new BIS paper on putting official statistics on a blockchain.
consp.read: The regulatory-capture frame, which is the standard and often correct read of any safety regime written by incumbents. The checkable kernel is the electricity one: large-load datacentre interconnections do shift transmission and capacity costs onto ratepayers in several US markets, and that shows up in rate cases, not just on message boards. The cartel claim about the mid-September session is inference about a meeting the White House says is not scheduled.

watch: Whether the Pickaxe Mountain threat converts. It was first made in mid-July and repeated tonight without being executed, which is the signature of leverage rather than of targeting. Watch for a strike, an IAEA access arrangement covering Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La, or a third repetition - the third repetition is itself evidence the threat is the product

The naming fight as a legal event, not a rhetorical one. The observable is a War Powers or Article II notification to Congress that uses the word war, or an authorisation vote actually scheduled. Absent either, 'military conflict' is doing exactly the work it is designed to do and the framing holds through the midterms

The next Bab al-Mandab transit count, because it is still the number arguing against us. Lloyd's List Intelligence, publishing JMIC data, logged 202 traceable transits between 24 and 30 August against at least 302 the week before and a 273-a-week August average. A second consecutive week near 200 kills our discriminating-blockade read; a recovery above 273 restores it

Gatun Lake against its rule curve, not the Panama transit number. Slots went to 34 a day on 3 September and drop to 32 on 15 September; the transit count is the output, the reservoir level is the constraint. October and November rainfall decides whether this is one El Nino season or the start of a structural watershed problem

The mid-September US-China AI session and the 24 September summit. Reuters says Bessent leads it and names He Lifeng as the likely Chinese counterpart with Ding Xuexiang as an alternative; a White House official says no such meeting is planned. A named Chinese principal, or a published information-sharing mechanism, turns a floated channel into an instrument

Whether the Witkoff and Kushner plane lands - Moscow on Saturday, Kyiv on Sunday. This remains our own dated falsifier on GEO-005, running to 14 September, and a trip is still not a term sheet. The observable that matters more is whether anyone tables a ceasefire-in-place text with a demarcation line both delegations acknowledge in public
lesson: Today's mechanism is eighty years old and it explains the diesel price better than any headline about tankers. In 1945 the economist Albert Hirschman published National Power and the Structure of Foreign Trade, and his argument was deceptively simple: the power one country holds over another is not measured by how much trade flows between them, but by how HARD it would be for the weaker side to replace it. Volume is not leverage. Substitutability is leverage. Apply that to oil and the whole story flips. Crude is highly substitutable - there are dozens of producers, and a barrel from Guyana burns much like a barrel from Basra - which is why the crude price is around $96 and calm-ish while the world's most important strait is contested. Refining capacity is NOT substitutable, because you cannot buy a distillation and hydrocracking unit off a shelf, and that is why the margin for turning crude into diesel just printed an all-time record of $108 a barrel while crude did not. Hirschman's prediction, restated for today, is that political power is quietly migrating to whoever controls the least substitutable step in the chain - which right now is not the oilfield but the refinery, and increasingly a refinery in India, the Gulf or China rather than in the West. It also predicts the behaviour we are watching: Russia banning diesel exports, Ukraine bombing refineries rather than wells, and Washington leaning on allies about a strait, are all the same move made from different seats - each side reaching for the bottleneck rather than the volume. Handle the theory honestly: Hirschman was writing about interwar German trade policy and his index has real limits, chiefly that it assumes states can perceive their own dependence, which they routinely cannot until the bill lands. But the test is scoreable and it is on our board as GEO-026 - if the diesel crack falls back under $45 before mid-December, the bottleneck was temporary and the leverage was borrowed; if it does not, the West has discovered a dependency it had not priced.

quiz.q: Crude is around $96 and off its highs, but the diesel refining margin just printed an all-time record of $108 a barrel. What does that combination actually tell you?
options: That there is less oil in the ground than the market believed
That the binding shortage is in refining capacity, not in crude - and refineries take years to build, so the constraint cannot be surged away
That speculators have cornered the diesel market
That OPEC has secretly cut production
quiz.why: A crack spread is the margin between a barrel of crude and the fuel refined out of it. When that margin sets records while the crude price does not, the scarce thing is the kit, not the geology - and that distinction is the whole story, because valves open in hours and refineries take years.

quiz.q: Katz said Israel will not leave southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout Lebanon. Why did the brief treat that sentence as the important one?
options: Because it is a threat to invade Beirut
Because it means Israel will withdraw within months
Because it violates the ceasefire text
Because it is a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to deliver, which turns a withdrawal into something that happens by decision rather than by completion
quiz.why: Watch the exit criterion, not the map. A condition no one can satisfy is not a milestone - it is an open-ended presence with a milestone's grammar, which is exactly how the 1985-2000 security zone worked.

quiz.q: The brief CUT the odds of an Israel-Hezbollah multi-week campaign on the day Israel declared a permanent security zone. What was the reasoning?
options: Because a held buffer historically produces chronic low-grade attrition instead of episodic campaigns - the 1985-2000 zone produced about two multi-week operations in fifteen years
Because Hezbollah has been destroyed
Because the ceasefire now has a third-party verifier
Because Israel's election makes any operation impossible
quiz.why: That base rate is roughly 13% a year for the escalation class, well below the 32% the book was carrying - and publishing a cut on an escalatory-sounding day is the test of whether a forecast follows evidence or mood.

quiz.q: Russia is reported to be trying to stop the US envoys continuing from Moscow to Kyiv. What does that behaviour most likely reveal?
options: That Russia is close to accepting a ceasefire
That Russia does not want to negotiate at all
That Moscow values exclusive access to the channel more than it values the meeting - a bargaining position rather than a peace position
That the envoys are working for Ukraine
quiz.why: Wanting the conversation to itself is a strong tell about intent. A party genuinely seeking convergence wants both sides in the room; a party seeking terms wants to speak to the guarantor alone.

quiz.q: CRITICAL THINKING. A widely shared claim says the diesel shortage is engineered - that US refineries were deliberately allowed to decay until scarcity was inevitable, and that America is exporting fuel out of a shortage. Which observable would most usefully test it?
options: Whether pundits on TV admit refining is a problem
Whether diesel prices go higher next month
Whether the government denies the claim
Whether the timeline of refinery closures predates the actors being blamed, and whether closure decisions track margins and complexity economics rather than any policy date
quiz.why: The checkable half of the claim is real - export flows and stretched maintenance intervals are documented. The engineered half needs a rail older than the crisis, and refinery closures driven by margin economics over four decades do not supply one. Testing a claim means finding the part that could fail, not the part that feels true.

plumbing.read: Today the physical leg and the monetary leg pointed the same way for the first time this week, and that is what makes it worth writing down. The physical print: US diesel at a record $5.820 a gallon, the crack at an all-time $108.02 intraday, East Coast distillate at a record-low 19.3 million barrels, August national stocks the thinnest since 1982. The monetary print: 162,000 August payrolls against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, into a Federal Reserve whose live debate is a rate RISE rather than a cut, and Waller leaning to hold only if inflation keeps improving. That combination is the manual's RESCUE WITHHELD class - a market certain the firemen are coming, in a shock the firemen cannot fix, because a policy rate does not build a hydrocracker. The long end has already priced it: ten-year 4.79%, thirty-year 5.27%, both above our published red lines, with the reverse-repo buffer at $0.70bn and effectively gone. What is STILL not printing is the milkshake tape - the broad dollar is 118.75 and soft on the month, so this remains a term-premium and supply-shock event rather than a dollar squeeze, and we say so rather than reaching for the more dramatic reading. Falsifier, dated: a diesel crack back under $45 before 15 December with the strait still contested marks this an outage, not a regime, and scores GEO-026 against us.
plumbing.epoch: E1 reopened - the 1973-79 oil-yoked-to-the-dollar rail, running now through its refining sequel rather than its crude one - alongside E6, whose September-2019 repo confession never closed (Fed still buying bills, ON RRP at $0.70bn), and E7, the weaponized-settlement rail opened by the 2022 reserve freeze and visible today in a Russian export ban and an Argentine sanctions decree aimed at a British-Israeli oil project.
